title: Double Smash Burgers
subtitle: Crispy edges, melty cheese, crew-approved
description: Crew Favorite · Comfort Food · Diner griddle night · Feeds 8+

ingredients.name: Frozen crinkle or diner fries
ingredients.notes: 4 lb Frozen crinkle or diner fries

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Make dirty sauce (no heat, 5 min): Whisk mayo, ketchup, mustard, relish, Worcestershire, garlic powder, and smoked paprika until creamy and pink-tan. Dirty sauce should taste tangy-savory-sweet — not plain mayo. Hold refrigerated until service; room-temp sauce on hot burgers is fine, but don't water it down.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Caramelize onions (medium-low, 25–30 min): Slice onions into thin half-moons. Melt butter in a wide pan over medium-low — gentle heat is the secret (high heat burns before sweet). Stir every 3–4 minutes until onions turn jammy, mahogany, and smell like candy (25–30 min). They should melt when pressed, not hold crunch. Season lightly with salt. Common mistake: rushing — pale onions taste sharp, not diner-sweet.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Prep & portion beef (no heat, 10 min): Divide beef into 2.5–3 oz loose balls per patty (16 balls for 8 double stacks). Do not pack tight — air pockets help the smash spread. Chill until smash time if kitchen is warm; cold fat renders into crispy edges. Shred iceberg fine; drain pickle chips on paper towels so buns don't sog.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Toast potato buns (medium, 4 min): Butter cut sides of potato buns generously. Toast on griddle or skillet until edges are golden and centers still soft — you want a glossy, buttery shell that won't dissolve under sauce. Toast just before smashing so buns stay warm. Stack cut-side up on a sheet pan.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Smash first patty — crust formation (high, 2 min): Heat cast iron or flat griddle until a water droplet dances and evaporates in 2 seconds — that's smash heat. Oil lightly. Place a beef ball, immediately smash flat with a stiff spatula (use parchment on spatula if it sticks). Press 10 seconds so meat spreads thin with lacy edges creeping past the ball. Season with salt and pepper. Don't move — crust is forming. Cook until edges look deep brown and lacey, top still pink-red, about 90 seconds.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Flip, cheese, stack second patty (high, 2 min): Scrape and flip with confidence — the crust should release cleanly. Lay American cheese on the cooked side immediately; residual heat melts cheese in 30–45 seconds (cheese should drape, not sit solid). Add a fresh beef ball on the cheese, smash again, season, and cook second crust 90 seconds. Flip once more, add second cheese slice, and stack both patties cheese-side-in so you get a molten core. Timing matters: cheese goes on the hot face right after flip, not before — otherwise it oils out.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Optional bacon (medium, 8 min): Lay bacon in cold pan, turn to medium, cook until shatter-crisp. Blot on towels — wet bacon steams the bun. Hold warm; add only at assembly so it stays crisp.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Bake diner fries (425°F, 22 min): Spread fries in a single layer — crowded pans steam instead of crisp. Bake until deeply golden with audible crunch when shaken. Season with salt immediately out of the oven (hot fat grabs seasoning). Hold in warm oven with door cracked.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Assembly order (no heat, 3 min each): Bottom bun → dirty sauce → shredded lettuce (barrier against juice) → pickles → double stack (cheese melted between patties) → spoon of caramelized onions → optional bacon → more dirty sauce on top bun → crown. Press lightly so stack sets. Serve within 2 minutes — smash burgers lose their crisp edge fast. Crew eats open-faced at the line if stacks are tall.

proTips: Smash once per side — re-smashing after crust forms tears the lace.
American cheese melts faster than cheddar; use it for that diner drape.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Toast buns in batches and hold in a warm pan — soggy buns kill the line.
Keep cheese slices under a dome so they melt fast when patties come off the griddle.
Line up Double Smash Burgers on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Store components separate — assemble fresh; buns go soggy overnight.
